subject: Pricing qualification & next steps - budget owner confirmation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@finex.ai>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 3:02 PM PDT
Subject: Pricing qualification & next steps - Finex intro call recap

Hi Aaron —

Great to speak earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align commercials with your finance/procurement team: 

Recap of what you shared:
- Primary workload: customer-facing chat + embeddings for search (user queries + semantic matching).
- Current expected steady-state volume: ~20M tokens/month (avg).
- Expected peak bursts during product launches: up to ~75M tokens/month for short windows.
- Key success metric: sub-200ms p99 latency for chat; cost per 1M tokens is an important input to your unit economics.

Pricing/volume info we covered:
- Target unit economics you mentioned on the call: aiming for roughly $250–$400 per 1M tokens depending on model/latency SLA.
- Given the 20M tokens/mo baseline, that maps to ~$5k–$8k/mo spent on inference (before discounts or reserved capacity).
- If you move to a reserved/dedicated configuration we can provide committed discounts and better predictability.

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm who the budget owner / economic buyer is for this workload (finance, head of engineering, or product)?
2) Will procurement/finance need an internal pricing checkpoint (legal/finance review) before we share a term sheet? Timeline?
3) I'll attach a pricing worksheet (attached) with a couple scenarios (on-demand vs reserved). If you can confirm the budget range that would let me pick the right commercial path.

Attached: redwood_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf (simple scenarios + commitment tiers)
HubSpot link: HS-789012

Proposed next steps: once you confirm the budget owner, I can loop in Rishi (for commercial approval) and Nikhil (solutions engineer) to prepare a one-pager and, if helpful, a simple committed pricing proposal.

Thanks again —

—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Aaron Li <aaron@finex.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 4:15 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Pricing qualification & next steps - Finex intro call recap

On Fri, Jul 10, 2026 at 3:02 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Aaron —
> 
> Great to speak earlier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can align commercials with your finance/procurement team: 
> ...

Thanks Marissa — super helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 20M tokens/mo is our conservative baseline; expected steady-state in 6–9 months is closer to 30M/mo. Bursts to 75M will be infrequent but real.
- Budget range: finance has tentatively allocated $6k–$12k/month for inference for the next 6 months as we validate. That aligns with the $200–$400/1M tokens band you noted.
- Economic buyer: our CFO, Priya Shah (pri...@finex.ai), will need to sign off on budget and contract. She likes to see a 3–6 month proof + clear unit pricing. 
- Procurement timeline: we hope to have finance review in the next 2–3 weeks; if pricing lands in the expected band we can move quickly.

Next steps from me: I'll introduce you to Priya and include a note on timing. Please include Rishi and Nikhil on that thread so we have the right folks for commercial and technical questions.

Appreciate it —
Aaron
Aaron Li | VP Product
Finex
aaron@finex.ai | +1 206-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aaron Li <aaron@finex.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, Jul 11, 2026 at 9:20 AM PDT
Subject: Re: Pricing qualification & next steps - Finex intro call recap

Thanks Aaron — that's perfect and very helpful. 

I'll wait for your intro to Priya and will prepare: 
- A short 1-pager showing a 3-month pilot scenario at ~30M tokens/month and the associated on-demand vs reserved economics.
- A proposed target price band to land in the $200–$350/1M tokens range depending on SLA and commitment.
- Any procurement materials your team needs (SOX/SOC2 notes, data residency, sample MSA language).

Rishi / Nikhil — looping you in as requested. If we land in the $6k–$12k/mo band, we should consider: 
- Offering an introductory committed discount for the first 3 months to accelerate proof-of-value.
- Flagging whether we need to prioritize lower-latency model variants (higher unit cost) vs cheaper model variants for embeddings/search.

Aaron — when you intro Priya can you include any specific procurement docs she expects? Also, if there is a preferred channel (Finance email vs procurement portal) please let me know.

Thanks —
—Marissa
